test_cases.test_name: Temperature Monitoring and Alarm Functionality Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the EMS continuously monitors temperature, records data at 5-minute intervals, and generates alarms when deviations exceed ±2°C from the setpoint.
prerequisites: EMS software is installed and configured
Temperature sensors are calibrated and connected
Test setpoints are configured in the system
User accounts with appropriate permissions are available

test_steps.action: Access the EMS software and navigate to the real-time monitoring display for a designated test sensor.
test_steps.expected_result: System displays current temperature reading for the selected sensor in real-time.

test_steps.action: Monitor the system for 15 minutes and verify data is recorded at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
test_steps.expected_result: System creates a new temperature record at least every 5 minutes as evidenced by the data log.
data_to_capture: Data log export showing timestamped entries
Calculation of time intervals between records

test_steps.action: Induce a temperature deviation exceeding +2°C from the setpoint using a calibrated simulator.
test_steps.expected_result: System generates an audible and visual alarm within 30 seconds of the deviation.

test_steps.action: Acknowledge the alarm and verify the alarm event is recorded in the system audit trail.
test_steps.expected_result: Alarm event is properly logged in the audit trail with timestamp and user who acknowledged it.
data_to_capture: Audit trail export showing alarm event
User identification of who acknowledged alarm

acceptance_criteria: Temperature is displayed and updated in real-time
Data points are recorded at intervals of 5 minutes or less
Alarms activate within 30 seconds when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint
All alarm events are properly recorded in the audit trail
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and audit trails
EU GMP Annex 11 for computerized systems
FDA guidance on process validation
data_integrity_requirements: All temperature readings must be time-stamped
Alarm events must be recorded in secure audit trail
Data must be stored in vendor's standard database format without modification

test_cases.test_name: System Integration and Alarm Notification Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the EMS properly interfaces with the facility management system and integrates alarm notifications with the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS is fully operational
Facility management system is available for testing
Site paging system is configured and operational
Integration protocols are properly configured

test_steps.action: Verify the EMS is communicating with the facility management system using the standard protocol.
test_steps.expected_result: EMS establishes successful connection and data exchange with facility management system.

test_steps.action: Send a test data packet from EMS to facility management system and verify receipt.
test_steps.expected_result: Facility management system receives and processes the test data packet correctly.
data_to_capture: Receipt confirmation from facility management system

test_steps.action: Generate a test alarm in the EMS and verify integration with site paging system via vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: Alarm notification is successfully sent to site paging system within specified response time.

test_steps.action: Verify the alarm message content and priority are correctly transmitted to paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: Paging system displays correct alarm message with appropriate priority level.

acceptance_criteria: EMS successfully interfaces with facility management system using standard protocols
Data transmission between systems occurs without errors
Alarm notifications are sent to paging system within 30 seconds
Alarm message content and priority are correctly transmitted
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic system interfaces
EU GMP Annex 11 for system integration
ISPE GAMP 5 for integrated systems
data_integrity_requirements: Interface transactions must be logged
Alarm transmission must be verified and recorded
Integration points must maintain data accuracy

test_cases.test_name: Audit Trail Functionality and Data Integrity Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system maintains a complete and secure audit trail for all critical data changes as required by 21 CFR Part 11
prerequisites: System installation completed
User accounts configured with appropriate privileges
System operational with sample data loaded

test_steps.action: Log into the system with administrator credentials and access the audit trail configuration settings
test_steps.expected_result: System displays audit trail configuration options showing all critical data elements are being tracked

test_steps.action: Perform various data modifications including temperature setpoint changes, user account modifications, and system configuration updates
test_steps.expected_result: All modifications are successfully executed and recorded in the system

test_steps.action: Access the audit trail report function and generate a report for the test period
test_steps.expected_result: System generates a comprehensive audit trail report showing all modifications with user identification and timestamps
data_to_capture: Verification of user identification for each action

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify or delete an audit trail entry using standard user privileges
test_steps.expected_result: System prevents any modification or deletion of audit trail entries with appropriate error message

acceptance_criteria: All critical data modifications are recorded in the audit trail
Audit trail entries include user identification, timestamp, and nature of change
Audit trail cannot be modified or deleted by users
Audit trail reporting function operates correctly
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures
EU Annex 11 - Computerised Systems
data_integrity_requirements: ALCOA+ principles must be maintained for all audit trail data
Audit trail must be secure and tamper-proof
All critical data changes must be recorded with user identity and timestamp

test_cases.test_name: Data Retention and Archival Capability Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system properly retains and archives monitoring data for the required 7-year period using vendor's standard features
prerequisites: System operational with historical data
Archival configuration completed
Backup storage media available

test_steps.action: Access the data retention configuration settings and verify the retention period is set to 7 years
test_steps.expected_result: System displays retention period configuration set to 7 years as required

test_steps.action: Initiate the archival process using the vendor's standard archival feature
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully archives data to the designated storage location without errors

test_steps.action: Verify archived data integrity by comparing original and archived data samples
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data matches original data with no corruption or data loss

test_steps.action: Test data retrieval from the archive by restoring a sample dataset
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully retrieves and restores data from the archive with full integrity

acceptance_criteria: System retains data for minimum 7 years as configured
Archival process completes successfully without data loss
Archived data maintains integrity and can be fully restored
Vendor's standard archival feature functions as specified
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures
FDA Data Integrity Guidance
EU GMP Annex 11
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be retained in original format without alteration
Archival process must maintain data completeness and accuracy
Restored data must be identical to original data

test_cases.test_name: System Performance and Response Time Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS meets the specified performance requirements for response time, data storage capacity, and system availability as defined in the URS.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and operational
Test user accounts with appropriate permissions are created
System clock is synchronized for accurate timing measurements

test_steps.action: Simulate an alarm condition by adjusting a sensor reading to exceed the ±2°C setpoint deviation
test_steps.expected_result: System generates an alert within 30 seconds of the deviation occurring

test_steps.action: Verify system data storage capacity by reviewing database configuration and projected storage requirements
test_steps.expected_result: System storage capacity is confirmed to support minimum 10 years of continuous monitoring data

test_steps.action: Monitor system uptime over a 24-hour period during normal operation
test_steps.expected_result: System maintains 99.5% availability excluding any planned maintenance windows

acceptance_criteria: All alarm conditions are responded to within 30 seconds as specified in URS-EMS-011
Data storage capacity is verified to support 10+ years of continuous monitoring per URS-EMS-012
System availability meets or exceeds 99.5% during the monitoring period per URS-EMS-013
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records reliability
EU GMP Annex 11 for computerized systems performance requirements
data_integrity_requirements: All performance metrics must be accurately recorded and timestamped
Storage capacity calculations must be based on actual data growth patterns
Uptime monitoring must include verifiable system logs
related_tests: OQ-001: Temperature Monitoring and Alarm Functionality Verification
OQ-002: System Integration and Alarm Notification Verification

test_cases.test_name: Standard Software Configuration and Vendor Feature Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS operates using vendor-supplied software without modification and utilizes standard features as specified in the URS.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed with vendor's standard software package
Vendor documentation for standard features is available
System is configured with default vendor settings

test_steps.action: Verify software installation by checking version numbers and comparing against vendor's standard release documentation
test_steps.expected_result: System is running vendor-supplied software without any custom modifications

test_steps.action: Test the vendor's built-in electronic signature functionality by performing a sample data review and approval process
test_steps.expected_result: Electronic signatures function correctly using vendor's standard implementation
data_to_capture: Audit trail entries for signature events

test_steps.action: Execute standard reports provided by the vendor and verify they contain all required data for batch release
test_steps.expected_result: Vendor standard reports contain complete and accurate data suitable for batch release decisions

acceptance_criteria: System operates using vendor-supplied software without modification as required by URS-EMS-003
Electronic signatures function using vendor's built-in functionality per URS-EMS-009
Standard reports provided by vendor are suitable for batch release per URS-EMS-007
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic signatures
GAMP 5 guidelines for standard software configuration
data_integrity_requirements: Software configuration must be verified against vendor documentation
Electronic signature implementation must comply with 21 CFR Part 11
Report data must be complete, accurate, and traceable
related_tests: OQ-003: Audit Trail Functionality and Data Integrity Verification
OQ-004: Data Retention and Archival Capability Verification
